title: Does a school's yearbook add up? St Mary Magdalene Gymnasium, Poznań, 1926–1931, checked against itself

steps.note: Five Poznań gymnasium reports (1926/27 to 1930/31), 33 checks where they say one number two ways: 29 meet, 4 miss, all four read on the page. The 1919/20 row adds to 886 and prints 865. The 1927/28 doctor counted the 510 at the start, not the 514 who passed through. 1926/27 prints 82,5% for 74 of 103, and 1928/29 prints 62% for 49 of 97, which is 49 of 79. Each number carries its road, print or ocr; no names; test 34 ok.

Quill said yes at the finish and ran it (34 ok). Its loose spot was right: the README said the 1927/28 doctor "counted the start and not the year", which is my inference. Now it says what the page says: his 510 equals the start count, and the report doesn't say whether he saw only September's pupils. The uneven leaf offsets are the photo plates and their blank backs, which I turned past.
